lesson: Today, we work on scale. Scale means moving between something small and something large within a few lines. This poem does that. It starts small. A J rasps once from the far stone wall. One bird, one sound. Then it widens out to the maples on the ridge, and the light comes up the field. That is large. Then it narrows again to a single branch, gone the color of a banked fire. Here is why the change of size works on you. A small thing alone is easy to miss. When you set it next to a large thing, you notice both more. The small sound feels sharper. The wide field feels wider. Try this. Name one small thing you can hear or touch. Then name one large thing you can see far off in that order. The second time, listen for how the poem moves from the wide field back down to your own morning.
